X-Request-Id.description: The request's id, on every response including refusals. Quote it when reporting a problem; the server's logs are keyed by it.

AssistantMessage.description: `content` is null on a pure tool-call turn, as OpenAI shapes it.
AssistantMessage.title: AssistantMessage

ChatCompletionRequest.description:
Unknown fields are ignored, as OpenAI does (the versioning rule in
reverse: a client may send what a newer OpenAI defines).
ChatCompletionRequest.title: ChatCompletionRequest

ContentPart.description:
One element of the array-of-parts content form. `text` and
`image_url` are accepted; an image goes to the gateway only when the
model takes images (`message_content`), and the rest are refused by
name.
ContentPart.title: ContentPart

ContextEvent.description:
Each count is null when the server does not know it: the window when
the model states none, the counts when the upstream reported no usage.
ContextEvent.title: ContextEvent

ConversationMessage.description:
A message as the conversation routes return it (`store.Message.to_dict`):
`parts` is the typed list the renderer maps, `content` the same text flat.
ConversationMessage.title: ConversationMessage

DeltaEvent.description:
Text for the open part at `index`: `content` for a text part,
`reasoning` for a reasoning part; one of the two.
DeltaEvent.title: DeltaEvent

EmbeddingsRequest.description:
OpenAI's `POST /v1/embeddings` body. `model` is accepted for client
compatibility (every SDK sends one) but the deployment's configured
embedding model is what goes upstream: there is exactly one, and a
caller naming another gets a 404 saying so rather than a gateway error.
EmbeddingsRequest.title: EmbeddingsRequest

ErrorEvent.description:
The turn failed after the 200. `code` is `budget` when the
organisation cannot buy the turn; absent for an upstream failure or a
resume that found nothing to resume.
ErrorEvent.title: ErrorEvent

ImageUrl.description:
OpenAI's `image_url` object: a `data:` URI or an `https://` URL, and
the optional `detail` hint, relayed to the gateway as given.
ImageUrl.title: ImageUrl

JsonSchemaSpec.description:
OpenAI's `response_format.json_schema`. The schema itself is relayed
untouched -- whether it is a schema the gateway can enforce is the
gateway's verdict, surfaced as a 400 with its reason -- but it has to be
an object, and it has to have the name OpenAI requires.
JsonSchemaSpec.title: JsonSchemaSpec

Metadata.description:
MatterWave's extras ride under `metadata`, which OpenAI reserves for
caller-defined key/values, so the request stays valid for any client.
`conversation_id` opts a call into persistence (stateless
by default).
Metadata.title: Metadata

PartStartEvent.description:
A part of the assistant message opens at `index`. A `tool_call` part
carries `id`, `name` and `arguments`; a `tool_result` its call's `id`,
`output` and `is_error`; `text` and `reasoning` only the index.
PartStartEvent.title: PartStartEvent

RequestToolCall.description:
A tool call the assistant made earlier in the conversation, echoed
back by the caller with its `tool` result -- the second half of the
round trip. Relayed to the gateway in the same shape.
RequestToolCall.title: RequestToolCall

ToolCallFragment.description:
One streamed piece of a tool call: the first for an `index` carries
`id`, `type` and the name, the rest carry `arguments` to concatenate.
ToolCallFragment.title: ToolCallFragment

ToolSpec.description:
One `tools[]` entry. Function tools only, which is all OpenAI's chat
completions define; the shape is relayed to the gateway as given.
ToolSpec.title: ToolSpec

apiKey.description: A MatterWave API key (`mw_...`), created under Settings > API keys. A key carries scopes; the one each operation needs is listed on it. Known scopes: `chat:read`, `chat:write`.

info.description: The OpenAI-compatible front door. Change `base_url` to this host's `/v1`, present a MatterWave API key as a bearer token, and every OpenAI client works unmodified. Every refusal is OpenAI's error envelope; every response carries `X-Request-Id`, the id to quote when reporting a problem.
info.title: MatterWave API

x-extensions.metadata.conversation_id: persist the turn into a conversation

x-stability.promise: Additive changes only within v1: no field is removed or retyped, deprecations carry Deprecation and Sunset headers with 12 months notice, and clients must tolerate unknown fields.

get.description:
What this API is and what it promises: the release, the endpoints,
what this deployment can do (`capabilities`) and the stability rule for
`/v1`. Needs no key, so a client can decide whether it can talk to this
deployment before it holds one.

200.description: What `/v1` is and what it promises.

post.description:
Send a conversation and get the model's reply, as one `chat.completion`
object or, with `stream: true`, a stream of `chat.completion.chunk`
events. OpenAI's request and response shapes; `model` may be omitted for
the deployment's default.

The request's `messages` are the whole prompt. With
`metadata.conversation_id` the turn is also recorded into that
conversation, but stored history is never added to the prompt: the
caller owns the context, as every OpenAI client assumes.

`tools`, `tool_choice` and `response_format` go to the model as sent and
what comes back is relayed: tool calls arrive in `message.tool_calls` (or
streamed `delta.tool_calls`) for the caller to run, never run here. A
`tool_choice` that demanded a call the model did not make is a 400
`tool_calls_unsupported`, not prose parsed as an answer.

requestBody.description: OpenAI's chat-completion request. Unknown fields are ignored; `functions`, `function_call` and `n` other than 1 are refused with 400 `unsupported_parameter` rather than ignored. `tools`, `tool_choice` and `response_format` go to the model as sent and what comes back is relayed: tool calls are returned for the caller to run, never run here. `metadata.conversation_id` records the turn into that conversation; the request's `messages` are still the whole prompt.

200.description: The completion. With `stream: false` one `chat.completion` object; with `stream: true` a `text/event-stream` of `data:` lines, each a `chat.completion.chunk`, ending in `data: [DONE]`. A failure after the stream has started is sent as an error envelope on its own `data:` line. With `stream_options.include_usage` the last chunk before `[DONE]` carries `usage` and an empty `choices`.

400.description: A malformed body (`invalid_value`), an unsupported parameter (`unsupported_parameter`), an image part (`unsupported_content_part`), a `tool_choice` that demanded a call the model did not make (`tool_calls_unsupported`), or a request the model gateway itself rejected, with its reason (`upstream_rejected`).

401.description: No key, or an invalid, expired or revoked one (`authentication_error` / `invalid_api_key`).

403.description: The key lacks the `chat:write` scope (`permission_error` / `insufficient_scope`), or the account is suspended (`account_suspended`).

404.description: A model the gateway does not serve (`model_not_found`), or a `metadata.conversation_id` that is not the key owner's (`conversation_not_found`).

429.description: More than 60 requests a minute on one key (`rate_limit_error` / `rate_limit_exceeded`, with `Retry-After`), or the organisation's monthly budget is used up (`insufficient_quota`).

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the next request.

post.description:
Turn one or more inputs into embedding vectors, in OpenAI's request
and response shapes. A deployment has one embedding model, so `model`
may be omitted; a deployment without one answers 404
`embeddings_not_configured`, and `GET /v1` says so in advance under
`capabilities.embeddings`. Usage counts against the allowance by the
prompt tokens alone.

requestBody.description: OpenAI's embeddings request. One embedding model per deployment: `model` may be omitted, and naming a different one is a 404. `GET /v1` says whether embeddings are enabled and which model (`capabilities.embeddings`).

200.description: One embedding per input, in input order.

400.description: A malformed body (`invalid_value`), or a request the model gateway itself rejected, with its reason (`upstream_rejected`).

401.description: No key, or an invalid, expired or revoked one (`authentication_error` / `invalid_api_key`).

403.description: The key lacks the `chat:write` scope (`permission_error` / `insufficient_scope`), or the account is suspended (`account_suspended`).

404.description: No embedding model is configured on this deployment (`embeddings_not_configured`), or `model` names a different one (`model_not_found`).

429.description: More than 60 requests a minute on one key (`rate_limit_error` / `rate_limit_exceeded`, with `Retry-After`), or the organisation's monthly budget is used up (`insufficient_quota`).

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the next request.

get.description:
The models this deployment serves, in OpenAI's list shape. Every
key sees the same list; which of them a plan may use is decided when a
completion is requested.

401.description: No key, or an invalid, expired or revoked one (`authentication_error` / `invalid_api_key`).

403.description: The key lacks the `chat:read` scope (`permission_error` / `insufficient_scope`), or the account is suspended (`account_suspended`).

429.description: More than 60 requests a minute on one key (`rate_limit_error` / `rate_limit_exceeded`, with `Retry-After`), or the organisation's monthly budget is used up (`insufficient_quota`).

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the next request.

get.description:
One model by id, in OpenAI's model shape. A former id (`grt-spark`)
is accepted and answers with the model it now names; an id this
deployment does not serve is a 404 `model_not_found`.

401.description: No key, or an invalid, expired or revoked one (`authentication_error` / `invalid_api_key`).

403.description: The key lacks the `chat:read` scope (`permission_error` / `insufficient_scope`), or the account is suspended (`account_suspended`).

404.description: A model the gateway does not serve (`model_not_found`).

429.description: More than 60 requests a minute on one key (`rate_limit_error` / `rate_limit_exceeded`, with `Retry-After`), or the organisation's monthly budget is used up (`insufficient_quota`).

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the next request.

/api/conversations/{conversation_id}/mes.description: Named events (`event:` plus one `data:` line of JSON), ending after `done`, `error` or `moderation_block`. `: mw-heartbeat` comments arrive between frames. The frames of the generation itself carry `id: <generation>:<seq>`; a client whose body drops re-sends the request with `Last-Event-ID` set to the last one seen and the server replays the rest of the same generation rather than starting another.

compaction.description: Earlier turns were folded into `message`, a `system` message with one `summary` part, before this turn was sent. Sent ahead of `message` when the next prompt would not fit the model's window.

context.description: The turn's real token counts, for a context meter; just before `done`, whenever the window or the counts are known. Carries `id:`.

delta.description: Text for the open part. Carries `id:`.

done.description: The turn ended; the saved assistant message, `truncated: true` and `finish_reason: length` when the model's token limit cut it.

error.description: The turn failed after the 200: the upstream died (what arrived is saved as a truncated message), the budget is spent, or a `Last-Event-ID` resolved to nothing.

message.description: The user message this turn appended (or the edited one), as saved.

moderation_block.description: MatterWave would not send this message to a model -- a different fact from the model declining to answer, so a different frame. Nothing was appended. `request_id` is the one to quote.

notice.description: Something the person should be told that is not part of the answer: a fold that could not run (`code: compaction`), after which the turn runs uncompacted, or a branch over the limit that an edit or regenerate cannot fold.

part_start.description: A part of the assistant message opens. Carries `id:`.

title.description: The conversation was named from this turn's first line.

/api/conversations/{conversation_id}/mes.order: (compaction | notice)? message title? (part_start delta* part_end)* context? (done | error)

/v1/chat/completions.description: Unnamed events (`data:` only), each a `chat.completion.chunk`. A failure after the headers is an error envelope on its own `data:` line, after which the stream ends; `data: [DONE]` ends a stream that finished.

message.description: One chunk, or the error envelope that ends the stream.
